message.content:
You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler, written in Rust), as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Your part: the MCP server, `bimcraft-cli mcp [--read-only] [FILE | --connect [PORT]]` — the JSON-RPC protocol over stdio on a headless session, and the bridge mode that forwards to a desktop window's control port.

## Hard rules (violating any of these fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (stdin/stdout/args/env/files/sockets are fine). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace it or try to read it. Never modify or delete it. NEVER run `./compile.sh`.
- No internet. Do not look for the program's source anywhere.
- Rust standard library only. Your code goes in `src/mcp/` (submodules as you like). Avoid editing other files; if you must, keep it minimal and say so.
- Scratch scripts (Python is fine, e.g. a fake window server) live OUTSIDE the repository, e.g. `/tmp/mcp-agent/`. Commit only Rust.

## The codebase (read first)
You are in a git worktree of the repo. `src/json.rs` (JSON `Value`, serde_json-identical parsing errors and float formatting; `.sorted()` sorts keys as serde_json::Value does), `src/session.rs` (`Session::new()`, `execute(cmd, params) -> Result<Value, String>`: snapshots, runs, checks, rolls back on error; `read_only` flag), `src/commands/mod.rs` (`resolve`, `changes_model`, `open_path`), `src/commands/basic.rs` (new/open/save…), `src/script.rs` (script parsing as `run --cmd` does), `src/catalog.rs` (the command catalog JSON that `commands` prints — `list_commands` likely uses it), `src/main.rs` (calls `crate::mcp::main(args)` for `mcp`). Many commands aren't implemented yet; build the protocol so each tool calls `Session::execute` (or the right function), and test with the commands that work (level, grid, new, open, save .bimcraft, undo, redo, delete) plus error paths. Build: `cargo build --release` in your worktree.

## What is known
- `printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' | /workspace/executable mcp` answers line-delimited JSON (keys sorted) with `instructions`, and tools `execute`, `script`, `list_commands`, `inspect_model`, `query_elements`, `schedule`, `render`, `new_model`, `open`, `save`. Learn everything: initialize variants and protocol versions, ping, unknown methods, notifications, malformed JSON, batches, ids of every type, `tools/call` results (content text, `isError`, `structuredContent`?), every tool's argument validation and errors, `script` with `atomic`, read-only mode (`--read-only` and `mcp --read-only FILE`), FILE opening (including .ifc/.rvt — `crate::commands::open_path`), EOF behaviour, stderr output, exit codes, argument errors (`bimcraft-cli mcp: ...usage...`).
- Bridge mode: `mcp --connect [PORT]` connects to a window's control port on 127.0.0.1; the port and a token come from `bridge.json` beside the favorites (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bimcraft`, else `~/.config/bimcraft`; `BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES` moves the folder — find out exactly). The README section "Drive it from agents, MCP and the CLI" describes it. Hidden tests run a fake window that records what the CLI sends; the expected request streams are in `/workspace/assets/test_mcp_connect/*.requests` (e.g. `{"op": "hello", "token": "…"}` then `{"command": "wall", "op": "execute", "params": {...}, "token": "…"}`; note `read_only`, `atomic`, how `render`'s optional args are sent as nulls, and that `new_model`/`open` are refused there). Write a fake window server in Python (in /tmp) to observe the original: what it sends for each MCP tool call, how it frames messages, how it reacts to replies of various shapes (success, error, missing fields, closed connection, wrong token), timeouts, and what it prints to the MCP client. Reproduce all of it. Use a temporary HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME when experimenting.
- `/workspace/assets/test_mcp/cabin.bimcraft` is a project a test opens with `mcp FILE` (it's a GUID-normalised saved file; find out how the original treats it).

## Targets (the hidden tests compare exactly, after GUIDs are renumbered by first appearance)
1. stdio protocol identical for every method/tool/error path you can find (with the commands that exist now; tool outputs that wrap unimplemented commands will improve as the core grows — structure it so they do).
2. Bridge mode: the exact request bytes for each `.requests` file's scenario and the replies printed to the MCP client.

## Testing tool
`MINE=<worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py -i <stdin_file> -- mcp` runs both programs in fresh temp dirs with that stdin and diffs normalised exit code, stdout, stderr and files (SAME or a diff).

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch. Final message: branch and commit, what matches, what doesn't, the bridge protocol as you found it, and what the core must provide (e.g. render returning a PNG).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

//! Scripts: one `id {json}` per line; blank lines and `#` comments are passed over.

use crate::json::Value;

pub struct Line {
    pub line: usize,
    pub id: String,
    pub params: Value,
}

/// Parses a whole script before anything runs, so a bad line stops it at once.
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Line>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (n, raw) in text.lines().enumerate() {
        let t = raw.trim();
        if t.is_empty() || t.starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }
        let (id, rest) = match t.find(char::is_whitespace) {
            Some(i) => (&t[..i], t[i..].trim()),
            None => (t, ""),
        };
        let params = if rest.is_empty() {
            Value::obj()
        } else {
            match crate::json::parse(rest) {
                Ok(v) => v,
                Err(e) => return Err(format!("line {}: bad JSON after `{}`: {}", n + 1, id, e)),
            }
        };
        out.push(Line { line: n + 1, id: id.to_string(), params });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

423-
424-`bimcraft-cli mcp` serves the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) over stdio, on a model of its own.
425-Add it to Claude Code:
426-
427-```sh
428-claude mcp add bimcraft -- /path/to/bimcraft-cli mcp
429-```
430-
431-or to any MCP client's configuration:
432-
433-```json
434-{ "mcpServers": { "bimcraft": { "command": "/path/to/bimcraft-cli", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
435-```
436-
437-| Tool | What it does |
438-|---|---|
439-| `execute {command, params}` | Any command with JSON parameters |
440-| `script {text, atomic?}` | Several commands, one per line; `atomic`: all or nothing, one undo step |
441-| `list_commands {filter?}` | The catalog, with parameters and shortcuts |
442-| `inspect_model` | Levels, counts, types, warnings and undo history |
443-| `query_elements {category?, level?}` | Elements with derived values: wall length and height, room area, door position |
444-| `schedule {name?, category?, fields?, filters?, sort?, grouped?}` | A schedule's columns, rows and totals; a new one, or one changed, as the command makes it |
445-| `render {view?, ceiling?, width?, height?, azimuth?, elevation?}` | A level's floor plan (or reflected ceiling plan), a section or elevation by name, a sheet by number, or with `view: "{3D}"` the 3D view, as a PNG the agent can look at |
446-| `new_model`, `open`, `save` | Projects; `open` imports `.ifc` files, `save` to `.ifc`, `.svg` or `.png` exports |
447-
448-A command that fails comes back as a tool error saying what to fix (`door: no wall at [4000, 3000] on Level 1`), and it
449-changes nothing.
450-
451-### On the project you have open
452-
453-Start the window with `--control PORT` (`0` for any free port) and an agent can work on the project in front of you instead of
454-a copy of its own: what it makes appears in the window, as an undo step you can take back, and is saved with Ctrl+S.
455-
456-```sh
457-bimcraft --control 0                       # the window says the port; bridge.json beside the favorites holds it and a token
458-claude mcp add bimcraft -- /path/to/bimcraft-cli mcp --connect
459-```
460-
461-`mcp --connect` takes the port from that file (or `--connect PORT` names it, which must be the window's). The port is on this
462-machine's own address only, a connection that does not say the token in its first line is dropped, and only the user can read
463-the file. The tools are the same, except `new_model` and `open`, which would replace your project: start or open another in
464-the window. The window answers between its frames, so a long command holds the window as it would from a button.
465-
466-File > Settings > Agents opens the same port without `--control` (and again at each start), on a port you choose or any free one,
467-and closes it. With **Allow agents to edit this project** off, an agent only reads your project: it inspects it, reads its schedules,
468-renders its views and exports it to new files (the sheets to PDF among them), and every change it asks for comes back as an error
469-that says so. The view control bar shows the port: off, listening on its number, or how many agents are connected, and read-only.
470-An agent's own side can ask the same: `bimcraft-cli mcp --connect --read-only`, or `bimcraft-cli mcp --read-only house.bimcraft`
471-for a headless server that opens the file and then only reads it.
472-
473-## Commands
474-
475-| Command | Shortcut | Parameters |
476-|---|---|---|
477-| `autosave` | | `path`: atomically write a native recovery snapshot without changing the project path or undo history |
478-| `recover` | | `path`, `project?`: validate and open a recovery snapshot; later Save targets `project`, or asks for Save As without it |
479-| `wall` | WA | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `top_offset?` (mm above `top_level`, negative below it), `height?`, `base_offset?`, `arc?` (degrees each turns, counter-clockwise), `location?` (`centre`, `core-centre`, `exterior-finish`, `interior-finish`, `exterior-core`, `interior-core`), `attach_top?`, `attach_base?` (a roof or a floor), `room_bounding?` (false: rooms run past it, as Revit's Room Bounding off; `modify` turns it on and off) |
480-| `door` | DR | `at`, or `wall` and `offset?`; `type?`, `family?` (a door family's `type`, its first by default), `mark?`, `flip_facing?`, `flip_hand?` |
481-| `window` | WN | as `door`, plus `sill?` (a family's `Sill Height` by default) |
482-| `sketch` | | `lines` ([[[x, y], [x, y]], …]; an arc [[x, y], [x, y], [x, y]], its ends then a point it passes through): solves a sketch without making anything, the loops it closes into (outlines and their holes) and their area, or every problem with the lines it's about: ends no other line meets, lines that intersect or overlap (a line that crosses itself too), three or more lines at a point. A sketch is solved as the straight pieces its lines are drawn with (an arc or a circle is cut into chords): past 200,000 of them it is refused at once |

content.content:
`BimApp::ask_file` (`dialog.rs`), never with a blocking `rfd::FileDialog`: a native dialog run inside the window's event
handler nests a run loop in it, and on macOS a drag reaching the window meanwhile re-enters the handler and aborts the app
(issue 43). The dialog (`rfd::AsyncFileDialog`) is begun on the window's thread, where AppKit wants it and where a sheet does not
block, and waited for on a thread of its own; `ask_file` is given what to do with the path, and `BimApp::dialog_answered` does it in a later frame (a cancel does nothing; one dialog is open at a time). A step
that goes on after a save (the unsaved-changes prompt's Save) is that `then`. A file dropped on the window is queued in
`opens`, as one the system asked for. A test hands the app a `Dialog` whose answer it sends itself (`tests/dialog.rs`).

The window's size (`window.rs`, issue 37) is `Settings::window` (its size in points and whether it was maximized, never its place:
Wayland tells an app none, and the window starts centred): `BimApp::watch_window` notes it once a frame, keeps it once it has held
still for half a second, and writes nothing for a window left as it started; `main` starts the window at the size the file holds
(`settings::window_in`). A window too big for its screen (the default 1440 x 900 on a laptop's, or a kept size after the screen
changed) is made smaller, once, in the first frame that knows the screen (`fitted`: 96% by 90% of it, never below the least a
window can be), and centred when it has taken the size.

The control port (`control.rs`, issue 41) is how an agent works on the project the window has open: `bimcraft --control PORT` binds
only 127.0.0.1, makes a token of 128 random bits and writes both to `bridge.json` beside the favorites (for the user alone; the
window takes it away when it closes), and `bimcraft-cli mcp --connect` runs its tools on the window's session. The protocol, and
what an agent may not do (`bridge::REFUSED`: `new`, `open`, `recover`, `highrise`, by any name, and a script is read through before it
runs), are `bimcraft_core::bridge`. A connection thread reads a line (at most 16 MB), checks the token, and hands the request to the
window through a channel; `BimApp::answer_agents` runs it in the frame as `BimApp::run` runs a button's command (`made_in`, then
`Session::execute`) and sends the reply back, up to sixteen a frame, and not while a file is being read or an update installed. A
request wakes the window (`Context::request_repaint`, from the context the first frame left in a `OnceLock`). Eight connections at
most; ten seconds, in all, to say the first line whole (a byte now and then does not count), and what is not a request, a web page's
HTTP say, is answered with an error and closed. A test (`tests/control.rs`) plays the agent on a real connection while the harness runs frames.

File > Settings > Agents opens the same port without `--control`: Let agents work on this project, and its Port (0 for any free one),
both kept in `settings.json` (`agents`), so the window opens it again at its next start once `--control` has had its say
(`listen_as_kept`), with the same bridge file and the same rules. Unticked, the port is closed: a `Control` dropped stops listening
(its accept thread is woken by a connection of its own and lets the port go) and hangs up on its agents, so it can be opened again.
Allow agents to edit this project (on by default, kept too) is `bridge::Access`: off, `answer_agents` runs each request read-only
(`Session::reading`), so an edit, an undo or a redo, a script holding one, or a save over the project's own file comes back as an
error that names the box, and what reads (inspect, schedules, render, exports to new files, the sheets to PDF) still answers; the
user's own commands are never read-only. An agent may ask to only read as well (`"read_only": true` in a request, which
`mcp --connect --read-only` sends). The view control bar ends with the port's state, in both profiles (`agents_indicator`): Agents:
off, Agents: port N, or Agents: N connected (a connection counts once it has said a request with the token), with read-only when edits
are off; a click opens Settings at Agents.

The interface's language is `lang::Lang`: a project's language, or Simplified Chinese (issue 38), which only the window speaks
(a drawing's lettering, `font.rs`, is drawn in code and has no hanzi, so a project is never in Chinese and `Lang::project()` gives
it English). Its words, including the schedule headings shown in the window, are in `translations/ui/*.po`;
missing or unfinished translations show English. Project text has separate catalogs; see [translations](translations.md).

shading or a rendering. Only the nearest see-through surface is blended, so a glass wall's far face and stacked glass don't
accumulate; plans and sections ignore it. Paint (`paint.rs`) is `{face: material}` in an element's `params` under `Paint`, a reserved
name: a triangle's face is read from its winding, so every solid emits triangles turned out (`Solid::tris`, `prism`), and
`Image::face` says which face a pixel is on. Favorites (`favorites.rs`) are a file of the user's own (`default_path`:
`BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES`, else the configuration folder) with materials and their pictures, families and their materials; they change
a project only through the `favorite` command (`load` never overwrites without `replace`). The desktop's Family Editor
(`editor.rs`) edits text (`FormText`, `ParamText`, ...) and changes the project's family only through a `family` command; its
preview is a scratch `Session` of its own, and it says what's wrong inside the window (the status box, over the view's corner, would lie on its
buttons).

A type of a category or of a family is renamed with `rename_type` (`Model::move_entry` moves it in its map, and `rename_entry` the
Updates (`crates/update`, drawn by `crates/ui-egui/src/updates.rs`). At startup the desktop asks `api.github.com` for the latest
release (`LATEST_URL`: never a draft or a pre-release) on a thread of its own, and compares its tag, `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, with the
running version as semver (`tag_version`, `is_newer`). Errors are quiet at startup and said in the status box when the user
asked (File > Check for Updates Now). A release whose installer isn't sound is still told of, with a Download button. The user's
choices are `update.json` beside the favorites (`Prefs`, `prefs::beside` the path `favorites::default_path` finds: `%APPDATA%\BIMCraft`,
`~/Library/Application Support/BIMCraft`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bimcraft` else `~/.config/bimcraft`, or the folder of the file
`BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES` names; the desktop's `main` hands it to `Updater::desktop`, because this crate doesn't depend on the core), never a project: whether to
check at startup, and the version they skipped (it and anything older are quiet at startup, a newer one is offered). The

assets as `Target::asset_name` does (`bimcraft-<version>-windows-x64.msi` and the other two) and publish them with `gh release

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Send lines to `executable mcp [args]` and show stdout lines, stderr and exit code.
usage: rpc.py [-m] [-a 'args'] [-d dir] [-r] line...   (-r: raw, lines given as python literals? no: given verbatim)
Lines: each arg is one line sent verbatim (a newline added). '@init' expands to the initialize request.
-m: use MINE instead of original. -b: run both and diff.
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, json, tempfile, shlex
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'
def run(exe, args, data, cwd, env):
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'mcp'] + args, input=data, capture_output=True, cwd=cwd, env=env, timeout=60)
    return p
def show(p, trunc):
    out = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    for l in out.split('\n'):
        if l == '': continue
        if trunc and len(l) > trunc: l = l[:trunc] + '...(%d)' % len(l)
        print('OUT:', l)
    if p.stderr: print('ERR:', p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'), end='' if p.stderr.endswith(b'\n') else '\n')
    print('EXIT:', p.returncode)
def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    exe = ORIG; args = []; both = False; trunc = 600; cwd = None; nonl = False
    while a and a[0].startswith('-') and len(a[0]) == 2:
        if a[0] == '-m': exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-b': both = True; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-a': args = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-t': trunc = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-d': cwd = a[1]; a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-n': nonl = True; a = a[1:]
        else: break
    lines = [INIT if x == '@init' else ('{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' if x == '@inited' else x) for x in a]
    data = ('\n'.join(lines) + ('' if nonl else '\n')).encode()
    env = dict(os.environ)
    if cwd is None:
        cwd = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rpc')
    if both:
        d1 = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rpcA'); d2 = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rpcB')
        p1 = run(ORIG, args, data, d1, env); p2 = run(MINE, args, data, d2, env)
        if (p1.stdout, p1.stderr, p1.returncode) == (p2.stdout, p2.stderr, p2.returncode):
            print('SAME'); show(p1, trunc)
        else:
            print('=== ORIG'); show(p1, trunc); print('=== MINE'); show(p2, trunc)
    else:
        show(run(exe, args, data, cwd, env), trunc)
main()
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drive `mcp --connect` against the fake window.

usage: bridge.py [-m] [-a 'extra args'] [-j bridge_json_override] [-w seconds_between_lines] ACTIONS_JSON line...
  ACTIONS_JSON: see fakewin.py ('-' for the default: hello ok then echo)
  Lines are MCP messages; '@init' expands to initialize.
  Prints CLI stdout/stderr/exit and the window log.
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, json, tempfile, time, shlex
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'
TOKEN = 'f00dfeedcafe0123456789abcdef0001'

a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
extra = []
bj = None
wait = 0.0
trunc = 1000
connect = ['--connect']
while a and a[0].startswith('-') and len(a[0]) == 2:
    if a[0] == '-m':
        exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-a':
        extra = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-c':
        connect = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-j':
        bj = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w':
        wait = float(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-t':
        trunc = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else:
        break
actions = a[0]
if actions == '-':
    actions = json.dumps(['{"ok":true}\n', {"default": {"echo": True}}])
lines = [INIT if x == '@init' else x for x in a[1:]]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='br')
xdg = os.path.join(d, 'xdg')
os.makedirs(os.path.join(xdg, 'bimcraft'))
portfile = os.path.join(d, 'port')
logfile = os.path.join(d, 'log')
open(logfile, 'w').close()
srv = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '/tmp/mcp-agent/fakewin.py', portfile, logfile, actions])
for _ in range(100):
    if os.path.exists(portfile) and open(portfile).read():
        break
    time.sleep(0.05)
port = int(open(portfile).read())
if bj is None:
    bjs = json.dumps({"port": port, "token": TOKEN})
else:
    bjs = bj.replace('PORT', str(port))
open(os.path.join(xdg, 'bimcraft', 'bridge.json'), 'w').write(bjs)
env = dict(os.environ)
env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = xdg
env['HOME'] = d
connect = [x.replace('PORT', str(port)) for x in connect]
work = os.path.join(d, 'work')
os.makedirs(work)
t0 = time.time()
p = subprocess.Popen([exe, 'mcp'] + extra + connect, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, cwd=work, env=env)
if wait:
    for l in lines:
        p.stdin.write((l + '\n').encode())
        p.stdin.flush()
        time.sleep(wait)
    p.stdin.close()
    out = p.stdout.read(); err = p.stderr.read(); p.wait()
else:
    out, err = p.communicate(('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode() if lines else b'', timeout=120)
el = time.time() - t0
time.sleep(0.2)
srv.kill()
for l in out.decode('utf-8', 'replace').splitlines():
    print('OUT:', l[:trunc] + ('...(%d)' % len(l) if len(l) > trunc else ''))
if err:
    print('ERR:', err.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), end='')
print('EXIT:', p.returncode, ' (%.1fs)' % el)
print('--- window log')
for l in open(logfile):
    print('  ' + l.rstrip('\n')[:trunc])

"""Drive `mcp --connect` against the fake window.

usage: bridge.py [-m] [-a 'extra args'] [-j bridge_json_override] [-w seconds_between_lines] ACTIONS_JSON line...
  ACTIONS_JSON: see fakewin.py ('-' for the default: hello ok then echo)
  Lines are MCP messages; '@init' expands to initialize.
  Prints CLI stdout/stderr/exit and the window log.
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, json, tempfile, time, shlex
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'
TOKEN = 'f00dfeedcafe0123456789abcdef0001'

a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
extra = []
bj = None
wait = 0.0
trunc = 1000
connect = ['--connect']
while a and a[0].startswith('-') and len(a[0]) == 2:
    if a[0] == '-m':
        exe = MINE; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-a':
        extra = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-c':
        connect = shlex.split(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-j':
        bj = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-w':
        wait = float(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-t':
        trunc = int(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else:
        break
actions = a[0]
if actions == '-':
    actions = json.dumps(['{"ok":true}\n', {"default": {"echo": True}}])
lines = [INIT if x == '@init' else x for x in a[1:]]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='br')
xdg = os.path.join(d, 'xdg')
os.makedirs(os.path.join(xdg, 'bimcraft'))
portfile = os.path.join(d, 'port')
logfile = os.path.join(d, 'log')
open(logfile, 'w').close()
srv = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '/tmp/mcp-agent/fakewin.py', portfile, logfile, actions])
for _ in range(100):
    if os.path.exists(portfile) and open(portfile).read():
        break
    time.sleep(0.05)
port = int(open(portfile).read())
if bj is None:
    bjs = json.dumps({"port": port, "token": TOKEN})
else:
    bjs = bj.replace('PORT', str(port))
open(os.path.join(xdg, 'bimcraft', 'bridge.json'), 'w').write(bjs)
env = dict(os.environ)
env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = xdg
env['HOME'] = d
connect = [x.replace('PORT', str(port)) for x in connect]
work = os.path.join(d, 'work')
os.makedirs(work)
t0 = time.time()
p = subprocess.Popen([exe, 'mcp'] + extra + connect, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, cwd=work, env=env)
if wait:
    for l in lines:
        p.stdin.write((l + '\n').encode())
        p.stdin.flush()
        time.sleep(wait)
    p.stdin.close()
    out = p.stdout.read(); err = p.stderr.read(); p.wait()
else:
    out, err = p.communicate(('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode() if lines else b'', timeout=120)
el = time.time() - t0
time.sleep(0.2)
srv.kill()
for l in out.decode('utf-8', 'replace').splitlines():
    print('OUT:', l[:trunc] + ('...(%d)' % len(l) if len(l) > trunc else ''))
if err:
    print('ERR:', err.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), end='')
print('EXIT:', p.returncode, ' (%.1fs)' % el)
print('--- window log')
for l in open(logfile):
    print('  ' + l.rstrip('\n')[:trunc])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""For every catalog command: execute with {} (and with a bogus param set) in normal and --read-only mode."""
import subprocess, json, sys, tempfile, os
cat = json.load(open('/tmp/mcp-agent/catalog.json'))
ids = [c['id'] for c in cat]
paramsets = [{}, {"id": 999999}, {"path": "nonexistent_dir/x.bimcraft"}]
if len(sys.argv) > 1:
    paramsets = [json.loads(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]]


def run(args, lines):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='ro')
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'mcp'] + args, input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=d, timeout=600)
    out = []
    for l in p.stdout.decode().splitlines():
        v = json.loads(l)
        if 'error' in v:
            out.append('RPCERR ' + v['error']['message'])
        else:
            r = v['result']
            t = r['content'][0].get('text', '<%s>' % r['content'][0].get('type'))
            out.append(('ERR ' if r.get('isError') else 'OK ') + t[:150].replace('\n', ' '))
    return out


for ps in paramsets:
    lines = []
    for i, c in enumerate(ids):
        lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "execute", "arguments": {"command": c, "params": ps}}}))
    # each command in a fresh process would be best, but a session per command is costly; use one fresh process per command
    for i, c in enumerate(ids):
        n = run([], [lines[i]])
        r = run(['--read-only'], [lines[i]])
        n = n[0] if n else 'NONE'
        r = r[0] if r else 'NONE'
        tag = 'SAME' if n == r else 'DIFF'
        print('%s %s %s\n    N: %s\n    R: %s' % (tag, json.dumps(ps), c, n, r))
        sys.stdout.flush()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure how long the CLI waits for the window. usage: timing.py MODE [max_secs]
MODE: hello  -> window never answers hello
      req    -> window answers hello, never answers the request
      partial-> window sends a partial line and never finishes
"""
import socket, subprocess, sys, time, os, tempfile, json, threading
mode = sys.argv[1]
maxs = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
exe = os.environ.get('EXE', '/workspace/executable')
s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); s.listen(4)
port = s.getsockname()[1]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(d + '/bimcraft')
open(d + '/bimcraft/bridge.json', 'w').write(json.dumps({"port": port, "token": "tok"}))
env = dict(os.environ); env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = d
t0 = time.time()
lines = ['{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"inspect_model"}}']
p = subprocess.Popen([exe, 'mcp', '--connect'], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, cwd=d)
conns = []


def srv():
    c, _ = s.accept()
    conns.append(c)
    f = c.makefile('rb')
    l = f.readline()
    print('%.2f got hello %r' % (time.time() - t0, l)); sys.stdout.flush()
    if mode == 'hello':
        return
    if mode == 'partial':
        c.sendall(b'{"ok":')
        return
    c.sendall(b'{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}\n')
    l = f.readline()
    print('%.2f got req %r' % (time.time() - t0, l)); sys.stdout.flush()


threading.Thread(target=srv, daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(0.3)
p.stdin.write(('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode()); p.stdin.flush()
while time.time() - t0 < maxs:
    if p.poll() is not None:
        break
    time.sleep(0.1)
el = time.time() - t0
if p.poll() is None:
    print('still running after %.1fs' % el)
    p.kill()
out, err = p.communicate()
print('exit', p.returncode, 'after %.2fs' % el)
print('OUT', out.decode()[:500])
print('ERR', err.decode()[:500])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run commands (execute) in a fresh normal session, then print the undo history from inspect.
usage: hist.py 'cmd {json}' ...
"""
import subprocess, json, sys, os, tempfile
lines = []
for i, c in enumerate(sys.argv[1:]):
    cmd, _, rest = c.partition(' ')
    params = json.loads(rest) if rest.strip() else {}
    lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "execute", "arguments": {"command": cmd, "params": params}}}))
lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "insp", "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "inspect_model"}}))
args = os.environ.get('ARGS', '').split()
p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'mcp'] + args, input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=os.environ.get('CWD') or tempfile.mkdtemp())
for l in p.stdout.decode().splitlines():
    v = json.loads(l)
    if v['id'] == 'insp':
        d = json.loads(v['result']['content'][0]['text'])
        print('HISTORY', d.get('history'))
    else:
        r = v.get('result') or v.get('error')
        t = r['content'][0]['text'] if 'content' in r else r
        print(v['id'], 'ERR' if r.get('isError') else 'OK', str(t)[:200].replace('\n', ' '))

spec: {"args": ["--read-only"], "connect": ["--connect"], "bridge": {...} (PORT replaced),

TOKEN = spec.get('token', 'f00dfeedcafe0123456789abcdef0001')
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
srv.listen(8)

replies = [spec.get('hello', '{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}')]
lines = [INIT] if spec.get('init', True) else []

"""Run a bridge scenario from a JSON spec against the original (or MINE with -m), print everything.
spec: {"args": ["--read-only"], "connect": ["--connect"], "bridge": {...} (PORT replaced),
       "hello": "<reply line>", "steps": [{"call": [tool, args] | "line": "<raw mcp line>", "reply": "<line>" | null}],
       "init": true}
Output: MCP stdout lines, stderr, exit, then each line the window received (repr of bytes).
"""
import json, os, socket, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading, time
a = sys.argv[1:]
exe = '/workspace/executable'
if a and a[0] == '-m':
    exe = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
    a = a[1:]
spec = json.load(open(a[0]))
INIT = '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"t","version":"1"}}}'
TOKEN = spec.get('token', 'f00dfeedcafe0123456789abcdef0001')
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
srv.listen(8)
port = srv.getsockname()[1]
replies = [spec.get('hello', '{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}')]
lines = [INIT] if spec.get('init', True) else []
for st in spec.get('steps', []):
    if 'call' in st:
        tool, args = st['call']
        lines.append(json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": len(lines), "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": args}}))
    else:
        lines.append(st['line'])
    if st.get('reply') is not None:
        replies.append(st['reply'])
received = []


def serve():
    while True:
        try:
            c, _ = srv.accept()
        except Exception:
            return
        buf = b''
        while True:
            d = c.recv(65536)
            if not d:
                received.append(('EOF', buf))
                break
            buf += d
            while b'\n' in buf:
                l, buf = buf.split(b'\n', 1)
                received.append(('LINE', l))
                if replies:
                    r = replies.pop(0)
                    if r == '@close':
                        c.close()
                        received.append(('CLOSED', b''))
                        break
                    c.sendall(r.encode() + b'\n')
            else:
                continue
            if received and received[-1][0] == 'CLOSED':
                break


threading.Thread(target=serve, daemon=True).start()
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='scen')
os.makedirs(d + '/xdg/bimcraft')
bj = spec.get('bridge', {"port": "PORT", "token": TOKEN})
bjs = json.dumps(bj).replace('"PORT"', str(port))

env['HOME'] = d
for k, v in spec.get('env', {}).items():

connect = [x.replace('PORT', str(port)) for x in spec.get('connect', ['--connect'])]
os.makedirs(d + '/work')
p = subprocess.run([exe, 'mcp'] + spec.get('args', []) + connect, input=('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode(), capture_output=True, cwd=d + '/work', env=env, timeout=120)

trunc = spec.get('trunc', 400)

    print('ERR:', p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), end='')

    for root, _, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            if os.path.islink(full):

        d1 = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='sA')

            out.append('--- files: orig %s mine %s' % (sorted(fo), sorted(fm)))
        if same:

            if verbose:

        else:

            print('DIFF', c[0])
            print('\n'.join(out))

    print('%d same, %d differ: %s' % (nok, len(bad), ' '.join(bad)))

def run(exe, c, d):
    name, lines, args, setup, env, raw = c
    e = dict(os.environ)
    e.update(env)
    data = raw if raw is not None else ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode()
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'mcp'] + args, input=data, capture_output=True, cwd=d, env=e, timeout=300)
    files = {}
    for root, _, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            if os.path.islink(full):
                continue
            files[os.path.relpath(full, d)] = open(full, 'rb').read()
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), files


def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    verbose = '-v' in a
    a = [x for x in a if x != '-v']
    flt = a[0] if a else None
    nok = 0
    bad = []
    for c in CASES:
        if flt and not re.search(flt, c[0]):
            continue
        d1 = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='sA')
        d2 = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='sB')
        if c[3]:
            c[3](d1)
            c[3](d2)
        o = run(ORIG, c, d1)
        m = run(MINE, c, d2)
        same = True
        out = []
        for k, x, y in (('exit', o[0], m[0]), ('stdout', o[1], m[1]), ('stderr', o[2], m[2])):
            x = norm(str(x)).replace(d1, '<DIR>')
            y = norm(str(y)).replace(d2, '<DIR>')
            if x != y:
                same = False
                out.append('--- %s differs' % k)
                for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x.splitlines(), y.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=0))[:30]:
                    out.append(l[:400])
        fo, fm = o[3], m[3]
        if set(fo) != set(fm):
            same = False
            out.append('--- files: orig %s mine %s' % (sorted(fo), sorted(fm)))
        if same:
            nok += 1
            if verbose:
                print('SAME', c[0])
        else:
            bad.append(c[0])
            print('DIFF', c[0])
            print('\n'.join(out))
        shutil.rmtree(d1, ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.rmtree(d2, ignore_errors=True)
    print('%d same, %d differ: %s' % (nok, len(bad), ' '.join(bad)))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Replay the scenarios behind /workspace/assets/test_mcp_connect/*.requests with an exe and compare
the requests it sends (re-dumped as json.dumps(sort_keys=True)) with the files."""
import json, os, sys
sys.argv = [sys.argv[0]] + sys.argv[1:]
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('bsuite', '/tmp/mcp-agent/bsuite.py')
bs = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(bs)
exe = os.environ.get('EXE', bs.MINE)
want = {}
for f in os.listdir('/workspace/assets/test_mcp_connect'):
    want[f[:-len('.requests')]] = open('/workspace/assets/test_mcp_connect/' + f).read()
for s in bs.SC:
    if s['name'] not in want:
        continue
    code, out, err, win = bs.run(exe, s)
    got = []
    for l in win.splitlines():
        if l.startswith('LINE '):
            b = eval(l[5:])
            got.append(json.dumps(json.loads(b), sort_keys=True))
    g = '\n'.join(got) + '\n'
    print(s['name'], 'MATCH' if g == want[s['name']] else 'MISMATCH')
    if g != want[s['name']]:
        print(g)
        print(want[s['name']])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the CLI set TCP_NODELAY? The window delays its ACKs; with Nagle a request comes in two
pieces 40 ms apart, with NODELAY all at once."""
import socket, subprocess, sys, time, os, tempfile, json, threading
exe = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '/workspace/executable'
s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); s.listen(4)
port = s.getsockname()[1]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(d + '/bimcraft')
open(d + '/bimcraft/bridge.json', 'w').write(json.dumps({"port": port, "token": "tok"}))
env = dict(os.environ); env['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'] = d
log = []


def srv():
    c, _ = s.accept()
    TCP_QUICKACK = getattr(socket, 'TCP_QUICKACK', 12)
    buf = b''
    n = 0
    t0 = None
    while True:
        c.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_QUICKACK, 0)
        d_ = c.recv(65536)
        now = time.time()
        if not d_:
            break
        if t0 is None:
            t0 = now
        log.append((round((now - t0) * 1000, 1), d_[:40]))
        buf += d_
        while b'\n' in buf:
            l, buf = buf.split(b'\n', 1)
            n += 1
            log.append(('LINE', n))
            if n == 1:
                c.sendall(b'{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}\n')
            else:
                c.sendall(b'{"ok":1}\n')
            t0 = None


threading.Thread(target=srv, daemon=True).start()
lines = ['{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":%d,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"inspect_model"}}' % i for i in range(1, 5)]
p = subprocess.Popen([exe, 'mcp', '--connect'], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, cwd=d)
for l in lines:
    p.stdin.write((l + '\n').encode()); p.stdin.flush()
    time.sleep(0.3)
p.stdin.close()
p.wait()
for x in log:
    print(x)

content.text:
The MCP server is done and committed on branch `worktree-agent-a72bc6bb3098c35fb` (head `8dd0a46`, three commits). Every difference left between it and the original comes from core commands that don't exist or are incomplete, not from the MCP layer.

**How I checked it.** I ran three comparison scripts in `/tmp/mcp-agent/`:
- **stdio** (`suite.py`): 74 of 88 cases are identical to the original in exit code, stdout, stderr and files written. The other 14 differ only where the core is missing something (list at the end).
- **Bridge** (`bsuite.py`, against a fake window in Python): 53 of 53 scenarios are identical, including the client output and the exact bytes the window receives.
- **The five `.requests` files** (`reqcheck.py`): my replayed scenarios produce exactly the expected streams, and the original produces the same ones.
- `cargo test` passes and the build has no warnings.

**One edit outside `src/mcp`.** In `src/json.rs` the nesting limit was one level too deep; serde_json refuses the 128th nested container. I changed `depth > 128` to `depth >= 128` in two places. This also fixes `run --cmd` with deeply nested JSON.

**What the stdio side reproduces:**
- **Protocol:** only four methods exist: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. `initialize` accepts the 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26 and 2025-06-18 protocol versions and answers anything else with 2025-06-18.
- **Messages:** notifications and stray replies get no answer, and `tools/call` sent as a notification does not run. Batches, all the error codes and messages, and any type of `id` behave as in the original.
- **Input and output:** lines are trimmed of Unicode whitespace before parsing. Invalid UTF-8 on stdin ends with exit 1 ("stream did not contain valid UTF-8"); a closed stdout ends with "Broken pipe", exit 1.
- **Tools:** argument checks, pass-through rules, render's picture and caption, script results and `list_commands` filtering all match.
- **Atomic scripts** run in a history of their own and become one "Script" step; a `new` or `open` inside one keeps the script's own steps instead.
- **`--read-only`:**
  - Up front it refuses commands that would replace the project (new, open, recover, highrise), and undo/redo.
  - It also refuses any `path` naming the project's own file. Paths are compared after resolving symlinks and `..`, falling back to the text when the file is gone; hard links count as different files.
  - Anything else runs first, so its own errors still come back, then is rolled back and refused if it made an undo step or changed the project or its current phase.
  - A save to another file leaves the project's own path unchanged.
- **Arguments and FILE:** argument errors print as `bimcraft-cli mcp: …`. `FILE` is opened before stdin is read; `cabin.bimcraft` fails exactly as in the original ("…is not a BIMCraft project: expected value at line 4 column 10", exit 1).

**The bridge protocol as found:**
- **Finding the window:** `bridge.json` sits beside the favorites: `BIMCRAFT_FAVORITES` with its file name replaced, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bimcraft/` (used even if relative), else `$HOME/.config/bimcraft/`. Empty variables are ignored.
- **Reading `bridge.json`:** it must hold a whole-number `port` up to 65535 and a non-empty `token`; anything else gives the "no window has opened a control port" error.
- **Connecting:** no HOME at all gives "there is no folder for the bridge file here". `--connect PORT` must equal the file's port. The connection goes to 127.0.0.1 with TCP_NODELAY and waits forever (I confirmed over 20 minutes with no timeout).
- **Framing:** one JSON line each way, keys sorted, written piece by piece. The first message is `{"op":"hello","token":…}`, answered by `{"ok":{"app":"bimcraft"}}`. If that reply also says `"read_only":true`, the read-only note is added to the instructions, but requests are not marked.
- **Requests:**
  - Commands go as `{"command","op":"execute","params","token"}`; scripts as `{"atomic","op":"script","text","token"}`.
  - With `--read-only`, every request except the hello also carries `"read_only":true`.
  - `render` always sends its 11 known keys, with null for any not given.
  - `new_model` and `open` are refused locally; `ping`, `tools/list` and `list_commands` never reach the window.
- **Replies:**
  - An `ok` key (even null) is the result, printed as pretty JSON; a script's result is wrapped as `{"results": …}`. Otherwise a string `error` is the tool error.
  - Anything else: "the window's reply says neither ok nor error" or "…is not JSON: …".
  - Losing the connection gives "the window closed the connection" (plus the OS error when there is one); an invalid UTF-8 reply gives "the window did not answer: …".
  - A failed hello ends the process with exit 1.

**What the core must provide for the outputs to match:**
- **render** returning `kind`, `view`, `width`/`height` as whole numbers, `pngBase64` or `path`, and `azimuth`/`elevation` for "3D view". The caption is built from exactly these fields; `notes` are ignored.
- **The missing or incomplete commands:** a full `inspect`, `elements` with limit/offset/level and `returned`, `schedule`, `wall`, `autosave`, and `highrise` reachable from `commands::run`.
- **delete and modify:** `delete` must reject unknown ids ("delete: no element 999999"), and `delete`/`modify` must always record an undo step (`always_step`). Read-only refusals and atomic "Script" steps depend on that.
- **undo count:** must give "undo: `count` must be a whole number, got 1.5".
- **Loading files:** the loader must reject references that aren't GUIDs ("`GUID-189` is not a GUID…"), and IFC import is needed for `open` and `FILE`.

My code is in `src/mcp/` (`mod.rs`, `rpc.rs`, `local.rs`, `bridge.rs`, and `text.rs`, which is generated from the original's own replies). The fake window and comparison scripts are in `/tmp/mcp-agent/` and are not committed.
